result.summary: Splits the monolithic `CreateNewBlock_validity` miner unit test into four independent `BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE` instances: `package_selection`, `sigops_adjusted_weight_chunk_limit`, `basic_mining`, and `prioritised_mining`. Each test case constructs its own 110-block fixture chain using a shared `MineBlockInfoChain` helper. In `basic_mining`, test transactions are now instantiated declaratively instead of mutating a single shared transaction object across sections, and `submitSolutionOld7` now tests the exact error message.
result.problem: Subtests in `CreateNewBlock_validity` shared a single in-memory chain, forcing later subtests to inherit state from earlier ones and requiring manual adjustments to `Tip()->nHeight` between calls. In `TestBasicMining`, a single `CMutableTransaction` was mutated across tests, making individual assertions depend on field modifications from prior checks and complicating isolation and debugging.
evidence: Description notes that "the subtests share one chain, so each starts from whatever the previous one left behind, and the caller has to patch Tip()->nHeight between them."
Commit message notes that mining the 110-block chain in each test case is cheap because "the blocks use hardcoded nonces."
result.scope_notes: Pure test refactoring confined to src/test/miner_tests.cpp.
result.changed_since_previous: Added commit 13847d5543, which changes the `submitSolutionOld7` check in `MineBlockInfoChain` from `BOOST_CHECK_THROW` to `BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION` with `HasReason` to verify the specific deprecation error message.
result.card: Splits the monolithic CreateNewBlock_validity miner unit test into four independent test cases and eliminates state shared across test sections. Subtests previously shared an in-memory blockchain and required manual Tip()->nHeight decrements between runs, while basic mining checks repeatedly mutated a single transaction instance across assertions. Each test case now mines its own 110-block chain via a shared helper with hardcoded nonces, and transactions are constructed declaratively in place. The change touches only miner unit tests.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause miner unit tests to fail or pass incorrectly in CI.
